page: Microsoft Azure D248lds_v7 is an x86_64 server type managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 248 dedicated Intel virtual processor cores and 496.0 GB of total system memory. This architectural configuration maintains a 1:2 compute-optimized memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, targeting workloads that require substantial parallel thread execution rather than vast per-core memory capacity.

Integrated local storage is a primary hardware feature of this instance, delivering 15,120 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Premium Storage. The system does not include discrete GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured networking resources for external accessibility.

The qualitative profile of this server pairs dense central processing power with massive local storage volumes. By reducing memory capacity relative to core count, the server reduces overhead costs associated with unneeded RAM in compute-heavy scenarios. The onboard NVMe storage provides ultra-low latency data staging without relying entirely on remote network-attached disks.

Workloads aligned with the D248lds_v7 include parallel batch computing, distributed CI/CD compilation farms, data transformation and ETL pipelines, and temporary scratch disk-intensive analytical tasks where high processor thread counts and fast local NVMe read and write speeds are critical.
